text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SERBIA
NASA BORBA

- International community expects Serbia not to block opposition-held cities, to start constructive dialogue as soon as possible and not to obstruct independent media, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told Serbian opposition leader Vuk Draskovic in Bonn.
- Serbian power company EPS plans to raise electricity prices by 9.7 percent from April 1.
- Belgrade university council to hold its constituent session Wednesday night and discuss resignation of rector Dragutin Velickovic.
- Serbian arms factories' workers will not hold their protest Wednesday because they did not obtain the necessary police authorisation.
- Private BKTV station regional broadcasts will end on Wednesday under a decision of Serbian PTT denying the station broadcast links for areas south of Belgrade.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia and Hungary sign a military cooperation agreement during visit of Yugoslav Chief-of-Staff Colonel General Momcilo Perisic to Budapest.
- French Foreign ministry refuses to issue visas to a delegation of the Serbian Radical Party invited to attend a congress of the National Front of Jean-Marie Le Pen.
- Leader of Serbian opposition Civic Alliance of Serbia (GSS) Vesna Pesic accuses Serbian government of not being ready for economic reforms and democracy during her visit to Vienna.

- Two U.S. Congressmen confirm in a letter addressed to U.S. Congress that they received letters from Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic which show "significant differences between Serbia and Montenegro".
- Serbian Patriarch Pavle received U.N. Administrator for Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein in Belgrade to discuss future of the Serb people in the Eastern Slavonia region.

- Yugoslav-Czech trade could reach half a billion dollars within a few years it was said during visit of Czech economic delegation to Yugoslavia. Czech republic negotiating extending a $100 million credit to Yugoslavia .
- Electronics Industry from Nis EI-NIS plans to start production of television sets with Philips parts, talks with the Philips management to be concluded within a few days.
- Reuters organising open university in Belgrade's Intercontinental hotel for Yugoslav bankers and finance experts.
- Average wage in Serbia in February was 691 dinars which is 12.5 percent up on previous month, according to statistics.

- Serbian Tansportation Minister Svetolik Kostadinovic says work on trans-Yugoslav highway to start on February 23 with the construction of a 71km stretch of road from Horgos to Subotica and Feketici.
- Socialist Party of Serbia and New Democracy Party praise Serbian government on what it has managed to achieve in difficult circumstances in its three-year work.
- Association of Serbian journalists to discuss Wednesday the working version of the draft information law.
- A long-term programme for development of agriculture is soon to be adopted to create conditions for exports says Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic.
- The problem of nuclear waste is not alarming but it needs to be resolved, says director of Institute for nuclear sciences Vinca Miroslav Kopecni.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Clocks in Yugoslavia to go forward one hour on Sunday, March 30 to be GMT plus two hours.

- Montenegro's steel works Zeljezara Niksic is in a difficult situation pressed by shortage of dinars and foreign currency, small demand for steel and inflated stocks, says directdor Vojin Djukanovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- The list of the new government to be presented to the Yugoslav parliament for adoption Thursday is not ready yet and last minute changes could be expected before the parliament session.
MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin Information ministry refutes authenticity of letter of Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic published in the Washington Times on March 11. It says Djukanovic is not destroying Yugoslavia and Serbia and wonders why Yugoslav dailies which published the letter did not verify its authenticity.

- Montenegrin airlines to have first commercial flight in April. The Fokker C28 plane is due to come back this week from servicing in the Netherlands. The ownership status of Podgorica and Tivat airports remains unresolved which is why the Montenegin company has probles with parking and servicing of the plane at Podgorica airport.
- Four Montenegrin commercial vessels exempted from the U.S. sanctions regime against Serbia and Montenegro to leave American ports by May 10.
- New Montenegrin culture minister Goran Rakocevic visits daily and lays out the republic's new culture policy.
- President of Montnenegro's National Party Novak Kilibarda holds news conference over fraction struggles in his party, accuses ruling Democratic Party of Socialists of wanting to split opposition.
- Trade union of Montenegrin port workers admitted to the London-based International Transport Federation.
- Montenegro will participate in Budapest spring tourist fair from March 19 to 23.

- Montenegro has power shortages due to long dry period and technical problems in power plant Plevlja. Domestic production covers only one third of the needs and the republic loans electricity from Macedonia, Romania and Greece.
